subject: MAP: performance QA plan and throughput + token-econ recap
summary: Mutual Action Plan focused on throughput benchmarking (sustained QPS, tokens/sec, concurrency) and resulting unit-economics. Includes test harness details, run matrix and attached CSV/slide results.
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Clarke <emma.clarke@ledgerly.com>, Ledgerly Platform Team <ops@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: MAP kickoff: perf QA plan + preliminary runbook

Emma / Ledgerly team —

Thanks for the time today. Per our MAP, attaching the high-level performance QA plan we discussed and the runbook we'll use for the throughput runs. High-level asks from your side: 1) sample request traces (anonymized) or tokenization examples, 2) approved test dataset (1000 representative requests), and 3) target SLOs for TTFT and latency.

Proposed schedule (MAP milestones):
- 2026-10-01: agree on run matrix and dataset (this thread)
- 2026-10-03: Redwood test harness provisioning & dry run
- 2026-10-05: sustained throughput runs (3 x 30min) across concurrency bands
- 2026-10-06: results analysis + unit-econ draft
- 2026-10-07: MAP sign-off + procurement next steps

Key evaluation axes:
- Sustained QPS (requests/sec at 95th percentile)
- Tokens/sec (aggregate across workers) and per-request token median
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) target and P95 latency for 128-token responses
- Concurrency bands tested: 8, 32, 128 concurrent sessions
- Unit economics: $ per 1k tokens and $ per sustained QPS (hourly)

Attachments (initial runbook stubs): map_runbook_v1.md (text), test_harness_spec.sh (script).

Next steps: please confirm dataset delivery by EOD 10/02 and your preferred time window for the sustained runs on 10/05.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Emma Clarke <emma.clarke@ledgerly.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ledgerly Platform Team <ops@ledgerly.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T10:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: perf QA plan + preliminary runbook

Soojin / Neha —

We can deliver a sanitized sample trace and the 1k request test set by 10/02 EOD (we'll push to the Drive link). Preferred window for the sustained runs is 10/05 08:00–12:00 PT. A couple quick clarifications before you run:
- Tokenization: we use SentencePiece, avg tokens per request ~ 95 (but distribution heavy tail to 450). We'll add token counts per request in the dataset.
- For TTFT, we care primarily about P50 for UI snappiness and P95 for SLA verification. Can you include P10/P50/P95 in the deliverable?

Also, procurement asked to see a short unit-econ estimate to include in our internal MAP worksheet — if you can include a $/1k-token and $/hour-sustained-QPS projection that would be great.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Clarke
Head of Platform Engineering | Ledgerly
emma.clarke@ledgerly.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Clarke <emma.clarke@ledgerly.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: perf QA plan + preliminary runbook

Emma / team —

Appreciate the token distribution detail — that helps a lot. Quick note on the harness and run matrix we'll use (details below). We'll run three sustained windows per concurrency band to capture variance and auto-retry behavior.

Test harness highlights:
- Worker fleet: 4 x A100-equivalent nodes (pinned), nginx fronting + continuous-batching enabled in runtime
- Model variant: open-v2-13b-quantized (the variant you validated in sandbox)
- Warmup: 5 min steady traffic at target concurrency to populate KV cache
- Metrics collected: tokens_out/sec, reqs/sec (qps), TTFT P10/P50/P95, latency P50/P95, GPU utilization, memory headroom

Run matrix (planned):
- Concurrency 8: 30m x 3 runs
- Concurrency 32: 30m x 3 runs
- Concurrency 128: 30m x 3 runs
- Each run replicates client-side arrival process from your trace and includes jitter to mimic production bursts

Acceptance thresholds (draft):
- Sustained QPS stable within +/-7% across windows for same concurrency
- TTFT P50 < 90ms, P95 < 220ms for 128-token responses
- Token loss / error rate < 0.2%

I'll kick off the dry run Thursday (10/05 08:00 PT) and post logs to the Drive folder. Rafael will be on-call for infra adjustments.

Neha
Neha Kapoor
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Clarke <emma.clarke@ledgerly.com>, Ledgerly Platform Team <ops@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: MAP results: sustained throughput runs + token-econ summary

Emma / Ledgerly team —

We completed the scheduled sustained runs this morning. Attaching the raw CSV and a short slide deck with the run-by-run breakdown. Key highlights (aggregated across the 3 runs per band):

- Concurrency 8: median QPS 68 req/s, tokens/sec 6,480 tok/s, TTFT P50 = 48ms, P95 = 120ms
- Concurrency 32: median QPS 275 req/s, tokens/sec 27,500 tok/s, TTFT P50 = 62ms, P95 = 165ms
- Concurrency 128: median QPS 452 req/s (sustained), tokens/sec 45,700 tok/s, TTFT P50 = 94ms, P95 = 210ms

Sustained behavior: the 128-concurrency band showed stable QPS within +/-5% across the three windows after the 5-min warmup. Error rate across all runs was 0.08% (mostly transient transport retries).

Unit economics (pro forma, based on your token mix and our dedicated offering):
- Measured average tokens/request (median) = 95 tokens
- Measured aggregate tokens/sec at target = 45.7k tok/s (128 conc) -> 164.5M tokens/hour
- Estimated cost assumptions used: GPU-backed dedicated cluster blended infra cost = $0.85/hour per sustained QPS-equivalent unit (internal metric), model execution and infra blended per-1k-token run = $0.018 per 1k tokens (Redwood internal cost estimate)
- Client-facing unit estimates (rounded):
  - $ per 1k tokens = $0.032 (includes infra amortization + ops margin)
  - $ per hour for sustaining 450 QPS (128 conc) = $380/hr (estimated list for Dedicated commitment; subject to contract)

Implications / recommended next steps:
1) If target is to sustain ~400–500 QPS, we recommend Dedicated pool with 6 pinned A100-equivalent nodes (current test used 4; 6 gives 25–30% headroom).
2) For latency-sensitive UI flows, enable prefix caching and tighter batching targets to improve TTFT P50 by ~10–15ms.
3) We'll draft a short MAP appendix showing the commitment tiers and the associated unit-econ buckets for your procurement team.

Attachments: ledgerly_throughput_results.csv (CSV, 145KB), map_performance_slide_deck.pdf (PDF, 820KB).

Subject: Re: MAP results: sustained throughput runs + token-econ summary

Soojin / Neha / Rafael —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the level of detail. The numbers look promising and align with our internal targets. A few follow-ups before we sign the MAP off:
- Can you produce a 1-page MAP appendix showing the recommended Dedicated commit tier and the explicit $/month for the Ledgerly expected 24x7 workload? Procurement needs that line item for PO prep.
- Can you include the CSV with per-minute aggregation so we can validate spikes at our end?
- Are there any licensing or support SLAs tied to the $380/hr estimate you provided?

Procurement will prepare a draft PO (PO-LED-1026) once we receive the MAP appendix. Please route the appendix and the per-minute CSV to ops@ledgerly.com and cc me.

Thanks — we'll aim to sign off by 10/09 if the appendix matches the projected spend.

Emma
